title: EMR debugging, monitoring, cost control
exp: Running your first EMR job and diagnosing failures end to end -- script upload to output verification and the debugging path when something breaks.
pts: Debug path: EMR console -> Steps -> failed step -> View logs -> download stderr from S3.
The Python exception is always in stderr for the failed step.
Common failures: wrong S3 path (FileNotFound), insufficient memory (OOM), missing IAM permission (Access Denied).
VPC Gateway Endpoint for S3: routes EMR-S3 traffic privately, free. Without it, NAT gateway charges ~$0.045/GB.
Right-sizing: monitor Spark UI executor utilization. 30% utilized means paying for 70% idle.
code:
#!/bin/bash
aws s3 cp orders_pipeline.py s3://my-bucket/scripts/

CLUSTER=$(aws emr create-cluster \
  --name 'OrdersPipeline' --release-label emr-7.0.0 \
  --applications Name=Spark --instance-type m5.xlarge --instance-count 3 \
  --use-default-roles --log-uri s3://my-bucket/emr-logs/ \
  --steps '[{"Type":"Spark","Name":"Process","ActionOnFailure":"CONTINUE",
             "Args":["--deploy-mode","cluster","s3://my-bucket/scripts/orders_pipeline.py"]}]' \
  --auto-terminate --query 'JobFlowId' --output text)

while true; do
  STATE=$(aws emr describe-cluster --cluster-id $CLUSTER --query 'Cluster.Status.State' --output text)
  echo "$(date): $STATE"
  [[ "$STATE" == "TERMINATED" || "$STATE" == "TERMINATED_WITH_ERRORS" ]] && break
  sleep 30
done

aws s3 ls s3://my-bucket/output/ --recursive
aws s3 cp s3://my-bucket/emr-logs/$CLUSTER/steps/ ./logs/ --recursive

viz.cap: Complete EMR lifecycle -- script upload to output verification

qa.q: Walk through debugging an EMR Step that failed.
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** EMR console -> Steps -> click failed step -> note S3 log path. Download stderr: aws s3 cp s3://bucket/emr-logs/j-XXX/steps/s-XXX/stderr ./. The Python exception is in stderr. Access Denied -> IAM permission. FileNotFoundException -> wrong S3 path. OutOfMemoryError -> increase executor-memory.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Boxing allocates a System.Object header (16 bytes on x64) on the managed heap and copies the value type bytes into it. Span<T> is a ref struct allocated strictly on the execution stack, providing contiguous memory access without heap allocation or array copying.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Boxing inside a high-throughput loop generates thousands of ephemeral Gen 0 objects, triggering frequent GC pauses and thread pool delays. Fix: use generic collection interfaces (IList<T>) and Span<T>/Memory<T> for byte slicing.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Span<T> provides zero-allocation performance, but ref struct rules forbid storing it on the heap, as class fields, or across async await points (where Memory<T> must be used).

qa.q: What is a VPC Gateway Endpoint for S3 and why save money?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Without it, EMR-to-S3 traffic routes through a NAT gateway at ~$0.045/GB even though both are within AWS. A VPC endpoint routes directly through the AWS backbone at zero cost. On 10TB/day this saves ~$450/day. One-time setup, no code changes.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Transient creates a new instance on every request; Scoped creates one instance per HTTP request container; Singleton lives for the app domain lifespan. Capturing a Scoped service inside a Singleton captures the DbContext across requests, causing concurrency bugs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Instantiating new HttpClient() instances manually causes socket exhaustion in OS TIME_WAIT state under high concurrency. Fix: register typed clients with IHttpClientFactory to manage handler lifetimes and DNS refresh.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** IHttpClientFactory prevents socket leaks and manages DNS rotation, but requires explicit Polly retry and circuit breaker policies to prevent cascade failures during downstream outages.
